exposure: transvaginal surgical repair of RVF and ASD with complete excision of fibrous scar and anatomical tissue layers reconstruction, aided by prior ultrasonography
cohort: The cohort consisted of 23 patients who underwent transvaginal surgical repair of rectovaginal fistula (RVF) and anal sphincter damage (ASD), primarily due to obstetric trauma.
finding: Complete excision of the fibrous scar and accurate anatomical tissue layers reconstruction of obstetric RVF or ASD, aided by prior ultrasonography, yielded good results, with all patients achieving full continence after 8 months minimum follow-up.
